title: Client retry governance & idempotency heuristics for multi-region failover
creator: Sofia Chen
description:
Problem statement: Cross-service retry and backoff semantics are inconsistent across Redwood services and client SDKs. This causes cascading retries during partial outages, inconsistent idempotency behaviour when failover happens, and poor observability for hedged requests. Goal: Define a lightweight, cross-service contract for retry windows, backoff profiles, idempotency key semantics, and hedging that works for multi-region failover while respecting SLOs and enabling predictable load shedding and circuit-breaker behaviour.

This ticket defines the governance, API-level headers, metrics, and rollout plan for client SDKs and runtime to converge on a single set of idioms that balance availability and safety during regional disruptions.
acceptance_criteria: Spec published in Confluence and linked to SDK repos
SDKs updated to emit agreed telemetry and respect header defaults
Runtime honors idempotency header for safe hedging and cancels secondary hedged calls on primary success
Chaos regression tests demonstrate no increase in duplicate side effects for idempotent operations
implementation_notes: Introduce optional X-Redwood-Idempotency header semantics: key + optional ttl_seconds; default ttl_seconds = 300
Hedging: client may issue at most one hedged request per logical call; hedged delay configurable and default to 50ms or adaptive relative to p50 latency
Backoff profile: use capped exponential backoff with jitter. Recommended: initial=20ms, multiplier=2.0, max=2000ms, jitter=full (rand(0,base)) for client transient retries
Circuit breakers: client-side circuit breaker per route + region with rolling-window error-rate threshold (default 10% errors over 1m) and cool-down 30s
Load shedding: clients should respect 429 with Retry-After header and degrade to cached responses or partial results where configured

Server contract: when X-Redwood-Idempotency present, runtime must guarantee exactly-once semantics for side-effecting ops when handler indicates idempotent=true; if not possible, return 409 with idempotency_conflict metric
rollout_plan: Week 1: Publish spec and RFC in #platform-reliability; gather design feedback
Week 2: SDK libraries (js/py/go) add default header handling and telemetry; feature-flag enabled in canary
Week 3: Runtime changes to honor idempotency header and hedging cancellation; deploy to staging + multi-region test cluster
Week 4: Canary rollout on 10% of traffic for low-latency routes; run chaos scenarios (latency spikes, region blackhole)
Week 5: Expand to 50% with monitoring thresholds; if duplicates > 0.01% rollback hedging defaults
Week 6: Full rollout and docs update; publish migration guide and cookbooks for service authors
test_plan: Unit tests for header parsing and TTL semantics in SDKs
Integration test: synthetic request with hedged=true; verify secondary cancelled on primary success
Chaos test: simulate regional failover while exercising idempotent create/update endpoints; assert no duplicate side effects
Load test: ensure backoff + hedging doesn't exceed configured partition throughput during recovery
comments: 2026-01-18 - Sofia Chen: Drafted initial spec and shared in #platform-reliability. Key open question: should hedging be enabled by default for low-latency read-only calls?
2026-01-25 - Rohan Gupta: Proposed adaptive hedging where hedged_delay = max(50ms, 0.2 * p50_latency) from the route's historical p50. Added to implementation notes as optional heuristic.
2026-02-10 - Priya Malhotra (review): Suggest tightening idempotency TTL for create operations to 60s by default and adding server-side dedupe cache size guidance.
2026-02-28 - Reliability SIG: Agreed to require SDKs to emit client.retries.total and client.hedged_attempts.total before canary rollout.
2026-03-12 - Rohan Gupta: Updated spec to include exponential backoff defaults and circuit-breaker thresholds. Created PRs for js/py SDKs and runtime.
notes: Tradeoffs: aggressive hedging reduces latency tail but increases load on upstream during outages; idempotency TTLs require storage/coordination cost on runtime to dedupe; adaptive heuristics recommended to reduce global defaults for high-throughput hot paths. Operational controls: per-customer hedging opt-out via account ini and server-side hedging budget with soft limits and fallback to single-call path.
